Ireland – Architectural design services – Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary
description: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. Tipperary County Council is undertaking a competitive tendering process for the establishment of a Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Multi-Disciplinary Consultancy Services for Public Realm, Landscape and Building Upgrade Projects in Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Framework Agreement will require the successful Consultant to provide, either directly or through its proposed multi-disciplinary team, all of the following services: 1. Architectural Services – Public Realm 2. Conservation Architectural Services 3. Landscape Architectural Services 4. Civil and Structural Engineering Services 5. Quantity Surveying Services 6. Project Management Services 7. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP) Services 8. Employer’s Representative Services 9. Public Liaison / Stakeholder Engagement Services 10. Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services 11. Planning Services 12. Archaeological Services 13. Fire Engineering Services Only Applicants capable of providing all of the above disciplines and associated specialist expertise, whether in-house, through subcontractors or as part of a grouping/consortium, will be considered. This competition will be conducted using a restricted procedure. At Stage 1, Applicants will be assessed against the suitability and selection criteria set out in the Suitability Assessment Questionnaire. It is intended that the five highest-scoring Applicants, subject to a sufficient number meeting all minimum requirements and rules for selection, will be invited to participate in Stage 2. At Stage 2, shortlisted Applicants will be issued with the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documentation. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the award criteria and weightings set out in the Invitation to Tender. The highest-ranked compliant Tenderer will be appointed to the Single-Party Framework Agreement and will also be awarded the Initial Contract. The Initial Contract will relate to the further development and delivery of public realm and associated projects in Clonmel. Clonmel Town Centre requires a significant streetscape and public realm upgrade. A design previously received Part VIII approval; however, the design now requires further development, amendment and coordination to reflect the current project scope and available funding and to bring the project through detailed design, tender, construction and handover stages. Tipperary County Council has also acquired a protected structure for which design development and a Part VIII planning process will be required. The Architect-Led Design Team may therefore be required to deliver a combination of public realm, landscape, civil engineering and building upgrade works, including works to protected and heritage structures. The Architect will act as Lead Consultant and will be responsible for coordinating and managing the full multi-disciplinary design team, programme, cost and delivery of the projects. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. Please note that an ITT is not required for this stage of the tender process.

buyer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Insourced Breast USC One-Stop Triple Assessment and Symptomatic Breast Radiology
description:
Hull University Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) on behalf of the Humber Health Partnership (HHP) plan to work in partnership with an Independent Sector (IS) Provider to facilitate provision of additional “one-stop” outpatient clinic capacity within the Breast Urgent Suspected Cancer (USC) pathway, to proactively manage capacity to maintain the delivery of the Cancer Faster Diagnostic Standard during periods where there is a demand vs capacity imbalance, and symptomatic breast radiology clinic support.

The “One-Stop Triple Assessment Clinic" is a new-patient outpatient clinic that delivers a triple diagnostic assessment in the form of:
• Clinical assessment
• Mammography and/or ultrasound imaging
• Fine needle aspiration or core biopsy

The IS provider will provide a full team of appropriately qualified and experienced workforce for each Breast USC “one-stop” triple assessment outpatient clinic (1 at Castle Hill Hospital and 1 at Diana Princess of Wales Hospital), namely for each site:
• 1 x Breast surgery clinician
• 1 x Radiology clinician
• 1 x Radiographer
• 1 x Radiology Assistant (RDA)
• 1 x Appropriate Breast Healthcare Assistant (HCA)
• 1 x Registered Nurse (RN) Support
Each clinic will be an all-day 25 patient session, utilising both AM and PM clinics. Clinics are expected to be delivered between 08:00 to 18:00 only. The sessions will be arranged initially over the weekends with options to be explored for weekday sessions in the future if required.

The "Symptomatic Breast Radiology Clinic Support" requires the provision of an appropriately qualified and experienced consultant radiologist to support weekday activity. This comprises the imaging component of triple assessment for symptomatic breast imaging and will include reporting mammograms / digital tomosynthesis, ultrasound of breast and axilla with biopsy as required and marker placement. Post marker check mammograms will also need reporting where appropriate. This will focus on patients that are referred into the breast symptomatic service on the Consultant led pathway. The requirement is initially for Wednesday & Thursday clinics at Castle Hill Hospital.

The contract is expected to run with an initial term from 2nd January to the end of March 2027, with options to extend for up to another 12 months subject to demand and internal approvals.

Please refer to the full service specifications and other ITT Documents for further details.

title: Cistern Maintenance
description: Servicing of a three-cell chlorinated water cistern. This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Edmonton Institution, Edmonton Alberta. Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: Lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to service a three-cell chlorinated water cistern supplying both the drinking water and fire protection systems. The work will involve the following: Objectives: The Contractor must replace four (4) failed underwater isolation valves to enable full hydraulic isolation of each of the 3 cistern cells: consisting of two (2) 133,000-gallon storage cells and one (1) 58,500-gallon pumping chamber. Once individual isolation of the cistern's cell is feasible, the Contractor must proceed with cleaning and disinfection of the cistern, one cell at a time. This includes isolating, draining, cleaning, disinfecting and refilling the storage cells and wet cleaning of the pumping chamber. The work also includes conducting a visual inspection to document the condition and identify any required repairs. All work must be performed while the cistern remains in service. Deliverables: The contractor must provide: a) Contractor must deliver a documented list of found deficiencies, photographs, and video of the work completed and provided to the Project Authority via flash drive or other means of electronic delivery. b) Contractor must provide photographs and/or video including all the work the Contractor has completed under the project SOW. The Contractor is also required to include a documented itemized list of found deficiencies outside the SOW including recommendations, photographs, and/or video. All videos and photographs are to be provided to the Project Authority via a flash drive or other means of electronic delivery. c) The Contractor must print material to be required, double sided printing in black and white format is the default unless otherwise specified by the Project Authority. d) The Contractor must ensure printed material is on paper with a minimum recycled content of 30% and/or certified as originating from a sustainably managed forest. title: Sanierung und Erweiterung Kindertagesstätte St.Michael, Bietigheim - Rohbau-, Erdbau-, Entwässerungs- und Abbrucharbeiten
description: Die Gemeinde Bietigheim plant die energetische Sanierung und den Umbau der bestehenden Kita St. Michael. Durch den Umbau sollen die räumlichen Voraussetzungen für die Betreuung von insgesamt 10 Krippen und Kindergartengruppen geschaffen werden. Maximal werden 190 Kinder in der Einrichtung betreut. Hierbei sind aktuelle pädagogische Anforderungen sowie die Belange des Brandschutzes und der Barrierefreiheit zu berücksichtigen. Ebenso soll die Haustechnik komplett erneuert und an die Anforderungen an Nachhaltigkeit und Komfort angepasst werden. Das Bestandsgebäude wurde ca. 1975 errichtet und umfasst ein Kellergeschoss und Erdgeschoss. Über die Jahre wurden an diesem Bestandsbau diverse Änderungen vorgenommen und mehrere Erweiterungen angebaut, zuletzt 2017. Es werden einzelne Gebäudeteile und der Innenausbau inkl. Technik rückgebaut. Hierfür sind Sicherungsmaßnahmen notwendig. Das bestehende Tragwerk des ursprünglichen Gebäudes hat sich als nicht ausreichend tragfähig herausgestellt. Im Untergeschoss müssen Fundamente unterfangen werden und neue Fundamente für neue Wände erstellt werden. Nach den Rückbauarbeiten werden neue Mauerwerks- und Stahlbetonwände und Stahlbetondecken hergestellt. Die Grundleitungen werden rückgebaut und neu verlegt. Seitlich am Gebäude werden Abgrabungen hergestellt, mit mehreren Stützwänden. Die Kindertagesstätte hat nach ihrer Sanierung eine BGF von ca. 2500 m² und einen BRI von ca. 8700 m³. Es werden Rohbau-, Erdbau- und Entwässerungs- und Abbrucharbeiten in folgendem Umfang ausgeschrieben: Abbrucharbeiten: ca. 1700 m² Bodenaufbau, inkl. Estrich Rückbau Wandbeläge, Abhangdecken ca. 1000 m² Mauerwerkswände ca. 1500 m² Stahlbetondecken (Rippen und Flachdecken) ca. 220 m² Fenster Rückbau Containeranbau mit ca. 150 m² sämtliche HLS und Elektroinstallationen im Bestand (auch Grundleitungen) Erdbauarbeiten: ca. 2300 m³ Bodenaushub komplette Entwässerungsarbeiten Erdungsanlage Rohbauarbeiten: ca. 65 lfm Fundamentunterfangungen Streifenfundamente für Abstützungen, neue Streifenfundamente ca. 500 m² Bodenplatte STB im UG ca. 270 m² Bodenplatte STB im EG ca. 1500 m² Decken aus Stahlbeton ca. 1200 m² Wände aus Stahlbeton ca. 400 m² Wände aus Mauerwerk ca. 1500 m² STB Decken über UG, EG und OG Abdichtung auf der Bodenplatte

title: Peltisepäntöiden puitejärjestely
description: Peltisepäntöiden puitejärjestely Museovirasto, Suomenlinnan hoitokunta -osasto ("Hankintayksikkö") kilpailuttaa Suomenlinnan ja Seurasaaren kiinteistöjen peltisepäntyöt ("Palvelu"). Tavoitteena on perustaa puitesopimus, jonka kautta Hankintayksiköllä on mahdollista hankkia Palveluita tarpeidensa mukaisesti. Palvelua teetetään Hankintayksikön hallinnoimissa rakennuksissa, joissa sijaitsee toimitiloja, työtiloja, asuntoja sekä museorakennuksia. Palvelussa kiinnitetään erityistä huomiota kohteen kulttuurihistoriallisiin arvoihin, ominaispiirteisiin, materiaaleihin ja vanhoihin rakennustapoihin. Töitä tehdään eri aikakausina rakennetuissa kohteissa, ja niitä tehdään ympärivuotisesti. Palveluihin kuuluvat esimerkiksi: • vesikatteiden peltityöt kuten katepeltien asennukset ja saumaukset • syöksytorvet ja räystäskourut • ikkunapellitykset sekä hormien ja läpivientien peltiasennukset • peltikatteiden tiivistyskorjaukset ja kattoturvatuotteiden asennukset. Tarjoaja voi toimia toimeksiannoissa joko päätoteuttajana tai sivu-urakoitsijana. Työkohteet ovat vaihtelevia ja osa kohteista on hyvin pieniä. Puitejärjestelyn perusteella tehtävät työt ovat pääsääntöisesti tuntihintaperusteisena laskutustyönä tehtäviä erilaisia peltisepäntöitä. Töitä voidaan teettää myös erilaisilla urakkamuodoilla. Työnaikainen dokumentointi ja valokuvaus sisältyvät kaikkiin töihin. Valituilla toimittajilla on mahdollisuus käyttää Hankintayksikön järjestämiä, yhteyskäytössä olevia henkilöstötiloja Suomenlinnassa puitesopimuksen mukaisten toimeksiantojen aikana. Tiloista peritään vuokraa, joka sovitaan erikseen. Seurasaaressa ei ole yhteiskäyttöisiä henkilöstötiloja. Hankinnan kohde on esitelty tarkemmin jäljempänä tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä. PUITEJÄRJESTELY Hankinnan tuloksena perustetaan puitejärjestely. Kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden valintaperuste on paras hinta-laatusuhde, minkä perusteella Hankintayksikkö valitsee neljä (4) parhaat pisteet saanutta palveluntuottajaa, ellei kelpoisuusehdot täyttäviä tarjoajia tai hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia ole vähemmän. Mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia vastaanotetaan vähemmän kuin edellä on esitetty, valitsee Hankintayksikkö kaikki tarjoajat automaattisesti mukaan puitejärjestelyyn, mikäli kaikki Hankintayksikön tarjoajalle ja sen tarjoamille palveluille asetetut vaatimukset täyttyvät. Sopimuskausi alkaa puitesopimuksen (hankintasopimuksen) allekirjoittamisesta ja jatkuu kolme (3) vuotta). Lisäksi Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden jatkaa sopimuskautta yhden (1) vuoden optiokaudella. Yksittäiset tilaukset puitejärjestelyn sisällä tehdään kevennetyn kilpailutuksen perusteella. Puitejärjestelystä tehdyn sopimuksen ehtoja ja sisältöä noudatetaan kaikissa Hankintayksikön ja puitejärjestelyyn valitun tarjoajan välisissä suhteissa. Puitejärjestelyyn perustuva toimeksianto voidaan tehdä vain puitesopimuksen voimassaoloaikana. Tarjoajan on otettava huomioon, että puitejärjestelyyn perustuvia toimeksiantoja toteutetaan Hankintayksikön päättämän aikataulun mukaisesti, jolloin toimeksiannot eivät välttämättä jakaudu tasaisesti sopimuskauden ajalle. Hankintayksikkö hankkii Palveluita omien tarpeidensa mukaisesti, eikä Hankintayksikkö sitoudu vähimmäisostomääriin. Puitesopimus ei anna valituille toimittajille yksinoikeutta hankittavien palveluiden toimittamiseen.,

Laitteiden omistusoikeus säilyy Toimittajalla, ellei Tilaaja lunasta niitä palvelun päättyessä. Kaikki edellä kuvatut Palvelut ovat esimerkkejä ja kulloinkin Tilaajan tarvitsemat Palvelut määritellään sisäisten kilpailutusten tarjouspyynnöissä. Palveluiden sisältö, määrä, toimitus ajat ja muut vastaavat tiedot täsmentyvät sisäisissä kilpailutuksissa. title: 6515--AESCULAP STAINLESS STEEL SURGICAL INSTRUMENTS
description: This Sources Sought Notice is for the Fredericksburg HCC to determine sources for a comprehensive package of brand name or equal Aesculap Stainless-Steel Surgical Instruments to support a wide range of surgical specialties at the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center. The instruments consists of Surgical Instrument Containers with Lids, Baskets for Surgical Instruments inside containers with lids, Silicone Mats/Cushioning Pads for Surgical Instruments placed in the containers with lids, Snap On ID Tags for inside Surgical Instrument Containers, Identification Labels to be etched with Tray Names for the Surgical Instrument and Containers, and Instrument Stringers. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT announcement only. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research and obtain information from qualified businesses. This is not a request for bids, quotes, or proposals. All responsible sources must submit a capability statement addressing their capabilities, capacity, place of manufacture, and location which shall be considered by the agency. � This notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to ultimately award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. � Interested parties submitting a response to this inquiry must include the following information: Capability statement Name and address of company NAICS Code SAM.gov UEI number Business size (large or small) Place of manufacture Identify applicable socioeconomic categories (SDVOSB/VOSB etc.) any pertinent information which demonstrates the firm s ability to meet the above requirement An authorized distributor letter if the interested party is not the manufacturer Identify all the products on any schedule and provide the contract number. Identify open market products All responses shall be submitted no later than Monday, 10/24/2026, by 10:00 AM EST. Responses shall be emailed to: Tiara.White@va.gov. When replying, please include Sources Sought 36C24626Q0993 to ensure the email is reviewed in a timely manner.

title: Integrated Multi-Modality Transfusion-Transmitted Disease (TTD) Testing Systems for Armed Services Blood Bank Center-Europe (ASBBC-EUR), Landstuhl Regional Medical Center (LRMC), Germany
description: 1. Purpose The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is conducting market research to identify capable sources that can provide a complete, integrated multi-modality Transfusion-Transmitted Disease (TTD) testing solution for the Armed Services Blood Bank Center-Europe (ASBBC-EUR) located at Landstuhl Regional Medical Center (LRMC), Germany. This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and planning purposes only. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ), or an invitation for bids. 2. Requirement Overview The Government requires the supply, installation, validation, training, ongoing maintenance, software support and upgrades, technical support, and reagent/consumable support for three complementary testing platforms capable of performing the full suite of U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) required blood-donor screening assays: Immunohematology / ABO-Rh, Syphilis, Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Antibody Titer (example platform class: Beckman Coulter PK7400 or equivalent) Serology (example platform class: Abbott Alinity s or equivalent) � Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Antigen/Antibody Combo, Anti-Hepatitis C Virus (Anti-HCV), Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg), Human T-lymphotropic Virus (HTLV) I/II, Anti-Hepatitis B Core (Anti-HBc), Chagas Nucleic Acid Testing (NAT) (example platform class: Grifols Procleix Panther / Ultrio Elite or equivalent) � HIV, Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), West Nile Virus (WNV), Babesia Approximate annual volume is 6,000 whole-blood units (plus residual plasma and platelets as needed). All systems must be FDA Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER)-cleared/licensed for blood-donor screening. Dual-marked (FDA + CE) systems are preferred. FDA-only systems are acceptable provided they operate directly on German power sources (single-phase 230 V / 50 Hz) with no transformer required. Preferred approach: A single integrated multi-modality solution from one prime contractor (or formal teaming arrangement). If responding as a team, joint venture, or prime-subcontractor arrangement, clearly identify the lead entity, proposed roles, and commercial distribution authority for each platform. If market research demonstrates that a viable single-source or single-team solution is not reasonably available, the Government reserves the right to pursue separate Requests for Quotation (RFQs) / Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for individual modalities. 3. Site and Utility Constraints (Critical) Performance location is a basement laboratory at LRMC, Germany, with approximately 585 usable square feet available after existing laboratory functions remain in place. Key constraints that must be addressed in any response: Power: Single-phase 230 V / 50 Hz. Schuko connectors preferred. Respondents shall provide the potential continuous and peak power demand (amps and kilovolt-amperes) for every analyzer and any supporting equipment (uninterruptible power supply, water-treatment system, etc.) under full operational load. Water: All three platforms are assumed to require treated/purified water (reverse osmosis or equivalent, Clinical Laboratory Reagent Water or Type I preferred). Respondents must state exact water consumption footprint (gallons/liters per day) for each piece of equipment presented, purity specifications, estimated daily volume, and footprint of any required water-treatment system(s). Footprint: Provide exact dimensions, weight, and clearance requirements for all proposed equipment and any water-treatment equipment. Environmental: Ambient 18�28 �C, 20�80 % relative humidity typical. Confirm compatibility. Network & Data Infrastructure: Workstations will be equipped with standard RJ45 Ethernet network drops; all equipment data interfaces must operate within the existing DoD/DHA local area network environment, and no external commercial internet connections or vendor-installed wireless networks are permitted. 4. Contract Type Preferences Both lease (cost-per-test or cost-per-kit inclusive of reagents, ongoing maintenance, software support and upgrades, and technical support) and outright purchase solutions will be considered. The Government states a preference for leased equipment, particularly given the potential relocation noted below. 5. Potential Facility Relocation ASBBC-EUR may relocate to a new facility within the next 2�5 years. The new location will not exceed 50 km from the current site and, for planning purposes, should be treated as approximately 20 km. Respondents should address: How a lease structure would accommodate relocation or early termination. Residual value, buy-out, or transfer options for purchased equipment. Any additional costs or logistics associated with de-installation, transport, and re-installation at a new German location within the distances noted above. 6. Performance Location and Legal Framework All performance will occur on a U.S. military installation in the Federal Republic of Germany under the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA). All applicable host-nation laws and U.S. laws and regulations will apply. Respondents must confirm ability to perform under these conditions and identify any existing in-country service capability, parts stocking locations, or technical personnel based in Germany or the European Union. 7. Correlation / Validation and Start-Up Costs Respondents should note that correlation and validation requirements must satisfy applicable U.S./DHA blood-bank standards as well as host-nation (German) expectations that the laboratory must meet. All reagents, quality-control materials, and related consumables required for initial correlation and validation shall be treated as part of the initial setup / installation cost and are not included in the ongoing test quantities or reagent volumes under the contract. 8. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration Interested parties must possess (or immediately begin obtaining) an active System for Award Management (SAM.gov) registration. Because this requirement is performed in Europe, respondents are specifically requested to state whether they currently maintain an active SAM registration with a European or NATO Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code. If not, parties that intend to respond to a future solicitation should begin the registration process now. 9. Information Requested Interested sources are requested to submit a brief capability statement (not to exceed 10 pages) addressing: a. Company name, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and point of contact, SAM registration status, including any European/NATO CAGE code. b. Confirmation of FDA CBER clearance/license status for each proposed platform. c. Whether a single integrated multi-modality solution (or formal teaming arrangement) can be offered. d. Lease and/or purchase pricing constructs (rough-order-of-magnitude acceptable at this stage), inclusive of ongoing maintenance and software support/upgrades. e. Potential continuous and peak power demand (amps and kilovolt-amperes) for the full proposed configuration. f. Water-treatment requirements, purity specifications, daily volume, and footprint (all three platforms assumed to require treated water). g. Equipment dimensions, weight, and site-preparation needs. h. Current in-country (Germany/European Union) service, parts, and technical support capability. i. Experience installing the same or equivalent platforms in European military, blood-center, or hospital environments. j. Ability to meet a Not-Later-Than operational date of 27 September 2027. k. Approach to ongoing maintenance, software support, and upgrades throughout the period of performance. l. Confirmation that reagents and quality-control materials for initial correlation/validation are included in start-up costs. m. title: Kulunvalvontajärjestelmän ja siihen liittyvien palveluiden hankinta
description: Kulunvalvontajärjestelmän ja siihen liittyvien palveluiden hankinta Espoon kaupunki, Espoon Elä ja Asu Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Matinkylän Uimahalli, Kiinteistö Oy Tapiolan Louhi ja Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Keskuskeittiö (myöhemmin myös Tilaaja) pyytävät tarjouksia Kulunvalvontajärjestelmän ja siihen liittyvien palveluiden hankinnasta. Hankinnan kohteena on Espoon kaupungin sekä Espoon Elä ja Asu Oy:n, Kiinteistö Oy Matinkylän Uimahallin, Kiinteistö Oy Tapiolan Louhen ja Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Keskuskeittiön hallinnoimissa rakennuksissa sijaitsevien Esmikko-kulunvalvontajärjestelmien korvaaminen uudella kulunvalvontajärjestelmällä. description: Sources Sought: Euclid Creek Fishway Construction; W912P425X11LG SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE, RELEASED PURSUANT TO FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) PART 10: MARKET RESEARCH. By way of this Market Survey/Sources Sought Notice, the USACE-Buffalo District intends to determine the extent of firms that are engaged in providing the services described hereunder for the Euclid Creek Fishway. This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes only and does not commit the government to any further contract actions, i.e., solicitation and/or contract. Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in responding to this Sources Sought Notice. Not responding to this Sources Sought Notice does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposals (if any) that may be issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. This is not a solicitation announcement; this is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This Notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP); it does not guarantee the future issue of an RFP; nor does it commit the government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, this Agency will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that this Agency will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice; all costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the responding party's expense. At this time, proprietary information is not being requested, and respondents shall refrain from providing proprietary information in response to this Notice. Responses to this Notice will not be returned. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Notice does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this Notice. GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS: The purpose of this project is to construct a full width ramp with a series of 31 weirs and pools. These weirs are designed as an upstream-pointing arch with side slopes which concentrate the flow towards the center of the channel. Further design elements include a 4-foot-wide V-notch in the weir and 1.5-foot diameter boulders emplaced on the weir. The 31st weir (upstream most weir) will be constructed entirely of concrete the intent is to protect the less robust rock emplacements by breaking up incoming ice. Construction of the fishway will involve partial demolition and excavation of the spillway and underlying bedrock to anchor the fishway to the rock and replace the existing spillway. On the downstream end of the fishway the existing channel will be removed for a length of 150 feet. A four foot-wide embedded low-flow channel in the center of the fishway has been designed to provide sufficient depth of water and flow during normal low flow conditions to allow fish passage. A series of parallel transverse rock ridges that consist of 1�6� foot diameter stones will be evenly spaced along the length of the ramp to provide a series of pools and falls. This low-flow channel and rock ridges are designed to allow for the passage of fish and other aquatic life would occur. Contract duration is estimated at 10 months. The estimated cost range is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages, and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. NOTE: Total submittal package shall be no longer than 5 pages. Please only include a narrative of the requested information. Technical: The technical proposal shall be addressed in sufficient written detail for the Government to determine if the Offeror understands the technical aspects of the Government's requirement. Offerors shall demonstrate how they will comply with the following subfactors: Subfactor 1: Technical Capabilities: - Offeror shall submit a detailed technical approach demonstrating its ability to perform all requirements of the Performance Work Statement (PWS), including the full range of ground ambulance services required under the contract. - Offeror shall provide management and operational plans, including safety procedures, staffing, training, quality control, and transition/start-up timelines from contract award through full operational capability. - Offeror shall provide a contingency plan addressing staffing shortages, vehicle breakdowns, severe weather, communications failures, emergency evacuations, and continuity of operations. - Offeror shall demonstrate its capability to respond to multiple simultaneous emergency dispatches, peak workload periods, and installation training events while maintaining required response times. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to provide and sustain the required staffing, vehicles, equipment, and operational resources necessary to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day, 365-day emergency medical services. - Offeror shall demonstrate its understanding of and ability to comply with all applicable Federal, State of Louisiana, Department of Defense, DHA, Army EMS, OSHA, HIPAA, and other regulatory requirements governing contract performance. Subfactor 2: Personnel Qualifications and Staffing - Offeror shall provide a staffing plan identifying labor categories, staffing levels, work schedules, and surge staffing capability necessary to meet all Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements. - Offeror shall provide an organizational chart identifying key personnel, including the Program Manager, EMS Medical Director, Paramedics, and EMTs. - Offeror shall provide resumes for all key personnel demonstrating the education, certifications, licensure, qualifications, and experience required to perform the services outlined in the PWS. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to recruit, retain, and sustain qualified personnel while maintaining required staffing levels and minimizing vacancies to ensure uninterrupted mission support. Subfactor 3: Vehicle and Equipment Maintenance - Offeror shall provide a comprehensive vehicle and equipment maintenance plan demonstrating how ambulances and medical equipment will be inspected, cleaned, tested, and maintained in accordance with manufacturer recommendations and applicable regulatory requirements. - Offeror shall demonstrate its capability to maintain continuous operational readiness through preventive maintenance, equipment inspections, inventory control, and timely replacement or repair of vehicles and medical equipment. - Offeror shall provide procedures for documenting vehicle inspections, equipment maintenance, corrective actions, and quality assurance activities to ensure uninterrupted mission support. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to maintain operational capability during vehicle or equipment failures through contingency planning and resource management in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. Subfactor 4: Quality Management and Performance Assurance - Offeror shall provide a Quality Control Plan (QCP) demonstrating how contract performance will be monitored to ensure compliance with all Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements. - Offeror shall describe its quality management processes for identifying, documenting, correcting, and preventing recurring performance deficiencies throughout contract performance. - Offeror shall provide procedures for monitoring personnel qualifications, certifications, credentialing, mandatory training, and regulatory compliance to ensure continuous mission readiness. - Offeror shall provide a continuous quality improvement approach demonstrating how performance data, customer feedback, and operational trends will be used to improve service delivery and reduce performance risk. Factor 2. Past Performance: The Offeror shall submit with its proposal evidence of recent and relevant past performance under which YOUR company (the Offeror) provided the same or similar services in the public and/or private sector. Performance must have been by the Offeror (not by a subsidiary or sister company) either as the prime contractor or subcontractor. Offerors shall complete and provide the Project Summary Sheet (Attachment 1) on three (3) task orders or stand-alone contracts/purchase orders the Offeror will complete or has completed within the past three (3) years from the closing date of this solicitation that the Offeror considers most relevant in demonstrating YOUR company's (the Offeror's) ability to perform the proposed effort. Past Performance must be with the Department of the Army, other US Government departments or agencies, state and local governments and/or commercial/private sector clients. If the Offeror performed as a subcontractor on the reference project, the Project Summary Sheet shall explain what percentage and type of work that was performed by the Offeror as subcontractor. In the instance that an offeror submits more than three (3) Project Summary Sheets, only the first three (3) will be evaluated. Offerors shall use the attachment provided. Past Performance Questionnaires (PPQs) (Attachment 2) may be submitted (however not required) for each past performance reference identified on the project summary sheet (Attachment 1). Offerors shall ensure CPARs are finalized and reference the exact same projects detailed in the Project Summary Sheet. If a PPQ or CPARs was not received for any of the past performance references identified on the project summary sheet, the Government may conduct interviews to validate performance/quality information. A past performance reference will not be evaluated if it does not contain valid/current POC contact information, or if the POC provided cannot validate work identified on the project summary sheet. title: NX EQ Combi Oven
description: The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Combi Oven product line as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as �national�) Requirements contract. Combi Ovens are thermally insulated chambers used in cooking for warming, cooking, and baking food, typically fueled by either natural gas or electricity. Food service ovens have thermostatic controls, which turn the oven on and off and select the temperature at which the oven will operate, and, usually, a timer. Food service ovens may have complex, computer-based controls allowing a wide variety of operating modes. They may be freestanding or countertop units. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to meet all requirements for the solicitation. The objective is to provide Combi Oven to be used by cooks within the VA medical centers and facilities, Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). The period of performance is for a base of 12-months with four 12-month option periods. Please see the RFP and attachments for more information.

title: IRB Horizon TBIPS
description: The objective of this requirement is to provide professional services support to the Chief Innovation and Technology Office (CITO) to advance the modernization of the IRB’s case management and adjudicative support environment through the Horizons initiative. Under this umbrella, work may include a portfolio of related digital modernization projects intended to improve operational efficiency, service quality, sustainability, interoperability, security, and scalability. This work includes initiatives to modernize legacy recording and information-handling capabilities through more current digital approaches; to streamline the creation, organization, and management of electronic case files through increased automation and standardization; and to support structured digital tools that guide and assist decision-making workflows in a more consistent and efficient manner. Collectively, these projects are intended to help the IRB assess, design, validate, and implement modern digital solutions that reduce manual effort, support more resilient operations, and strengthen the organization’s transition toward a more integrated digital environment.

title: APN - CETEMT New Facility and Compound, CFB Uplands
description: Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform the Design-Builder of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Uplands in Ottawa, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow the Design-Builder to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design-Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project will include an Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.   Description of the Project and Services   This contract will provide the design and construction of the new facility and compound near the existing CETEMT (Counter Explosive Threat Equipment Management Team) compound at CFB Uplands. The new facility will be a single-storey building with an approximate footprint of 1,650 m2. It will include offices and workspaces, meeting rooms, maintenance garages and workshops, specialized spaces such as secure storage and a weapons vault, and support areas including a kitchenette, washrooms, and server rooms. The facility will be situated within a new exterior compound of approximately 6,500 m2, including parking areas.   The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract. ROM estimate for the total value of the MDB contract is approximately $17M. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.   Contract Number: 88076 Title: CETEMT New Facility and Compound Approximate Estimate: $ 17M Anticipated Posting: Q4 FY26/27 Description: Provide the Counter Explosive Threat Equipment Management Team (CETEMT) a new facility and compound on CFB Uplands in Ottawa, Ontario according to operational requirements.   Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a Design-Builder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated industrial security requirements of this project will be at FSC Secret. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing Design-Builders  early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, Design-Builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential Design-Builders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 88076; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca   Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Priscille Vumi Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 343-596-6289 Priscille.Vumi@dcc-cdc.gc.caBidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. description: *Please note that the ISC website will be available on September 23, 2026* ***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. Phase 2: - The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $500,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. - The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is up to 15 months (excluding submission of the final report). - Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 5 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 2 awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: Travel to Suffield, Alberta for prototype demonstration. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The challenge is to provide the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) a software solution to provide an airspace common operating picture so that it can plan, deconflict, and control uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) traffic, including their use of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum, in order to ensure the safe and efficient management of UAS to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Details: Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be Windows-based. 2. Allow a user to create and store flight plans, including radio frequency requirements. 3. Have a flight plan repository (database) that stores the 4D (3D + time) trajectories and spectrum requirements of all accepted flight plans. 4. Enable integration of supplemental data services such as crewed aircraft flight plans and weather. 5. Generate an optimal 4D flight path for UAS based on specific mission goals and physical limits. 6. Be able to check new flight requests against existing flight plans, airspace constraints (no-fly zones) and RF spectrum requests to detect conflicts and resolve them (via set priorities or a human decision). 7. Generate 4D blocks of deconflicted airspace (a "tunnel" or a "box") where a UAS is permitted to fly. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Analyze real-time data from UASs to prevent collisions and automatically adjust flight paths for UASs in controlled airspace. 2. Check in real-time whether a UAS is following its pre-approved, deconflicted trajectory. 3. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies. To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. Critical components and requested information for each Critical components are defined below: Critical components: 1. Radio 2. Ground control station (GCS) 3. On-board computer 4. Any software Requested information: i. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): Name of the original equipment manufacturer of the product being sourced ii. OEM URL: Provide the URL of the OEM iii. Software: Confirm if developed by Offeror or outsourced iv. Product name: Provide the OEM's product name v. Model number: Provide the OEM's model and/or version number of the product vi. Product URL: Provide the URL of the OEM product, model, and version vii. Country of origin IMPORTANT NOTE: For this challenge, kindly disregard the Attachment requirements detailed at Section D in the Web-Portal, and instead adhere to the following: - The attachment measures 8.5" by 11" with a maximum size of 10Mb. - Only the following formats will be accepted: JPG, GIF, TIF, PDF or PNG. - The attachment must be clear and legible. Note: Including an attachment is not mandatory, but forms part of the Additional Outcomes, which is scored up to 10 points. The Applicant (Offeror) acknowledges that it is within Canada's sole discretion to determine whether the attachment is removed or included in the Offer. Background & Context The CA is undergoing a generational modernization effort to address the evolving nature of technology, the changing character of conflict, and the unravelling of the geopolitical system. The transformative changes being made are conceptually described in the CA publication Inflection Point 2025. This document provides the broad context for modernization and directs the development and acquisition of key systems; in particular, it states: Key to this transformation is the integration of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, autonomous and uncrewed systems. These capabilities will support a wide range of functions, from intelligence analysis and predictive modeling to targeting and operational execution. The CA, in recognizing this need, has purchased foreign robotics and autonomous systems of varying quality and has identified challenges purchasing systems that meet operational requirements, in particular related to cold-weather operations, and that have stable supply chains. Further, purchases have, in the past, been constrained by limited manufacturing capacity of industry partners. To address this, the Government of Canada's recently released policy Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, emphasizes the need to develop a strong domestic industrial capacity to produce defence materiel. This policy directs the CA to seek solutions to operational problems through Canadian industry, which will both improve the CA's capability while providing the foundation of a strong defence industrial base able to scale production of quality defence material. To date, engagements with Canadian industry have revealed a wide variety of small/medium companies that have commercial technologies that could, with support, be tailored to military requirements.

title: Maplelawn Garden Wall Rehabilitation
description: The NCC is seeking qualified proponents to submit proposals for the rehabilitation and reconstruction of the historic Maplelawn garden walls located in the Ottawa’s west end at 529 Richmond Rd. The project seeks to complete the following objectives: 1.Rehabilitate both structural and aesthetic integrity of the walls. 2.Eliminate the risk to public health and safety. 3.Replicate and preserve the historic characteristics of the walls 4.Ensure long-term durability of the walls. 5.Protect the surrounding environment and collaborate with stakeholders.

title: Subscription to metal and minerals economic data.
description: The Department of Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) has a requirement to provide senior management with detailed and accurate information on gold, silver, platinum group metals (PGMs), and other precious metals, including price forecasts; projections on supply and demand components; scenario outlooks for precious metals markets; detailed information about gold mine operations and gold markets; and other relevant information. NRCan will require access to a subscription to proprietary precious-metals market intelligence, historical data, forecasts, investment analysis, and gold mine cost data covering gold, silver, platinum, palladium, rhodium, and related precious-metals markets. The work will involve conducting thorough, data-driven research and sound economic analysis of the gold, silver, PGMs, and other precious metals markets and produce datasets, reports, briefing notes, presentations, and other materials that will help inform policy decisions. NRCan will also require user support as needed for questions surrounding the data, the web-based platform, and plug-ins and other online tools if available within three (3) business days.

title: EW038-270709 - Northern Innovation Centre Conceptual Design Study – RFP
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Works & Government Services Canada (PWGSC) requires the services of an architectural firm (Consultant), acting as the Prime Consultant with a multi-disciplinary team of sub-consultants for the delivery of services required for this project. The facility will be located at the Invuik Satellite Station Facility located in Inuvik, Northwest Territories. The Inuvik Satellite Station Facility (ISSF) is an international, multi-use science and technology facility and is located approximately 200km north of the Arctic Circle. NRCan requires the consultant to investigate options of accommodating their program in a modular building vs typical northern construction. A Class C cost estimate and conceptual schematic options developed through this study to seek early project approval to determine the project’s future viability. NRCan requires Pre-design/ Functional Programming and Schematic services to support preliminary costing and design work for a new multi-use modular facility of approximately 1,277m², excluding supporting areas to be proposed by the Prime Consultant and team. For this project, scope is limited to NRCan program requirements only, with future stakeholder participation or expansion to be considered separately once confirmed. Project stakeholder requirements are outlined within the Terms of Reference. See the Terms of Reference for more details.

title: Piste cyclable Hegi, de la Talacker-Strasse à la Solarstrasse, nouvelle construction – prestations d'ingénierie civile
description:
Le projet porte sur la construction d’une nouvelle voie piétonne et cyclable continue d’environ 1,1 km, reliant la Talacker-Strasse à la Solarstrasse. Le tracé passe au nord de la ligne ferroviaire et traverse des terrains appartenant aux CFF et des zones industrielles, ainsi que des pistes cyclables et des trottoirs existants qui devront être adaptés.


Le tracé se compose d’une chaussée de 4,30 m de large, dotée d’un revêtement teinté en rouge pour la circulation cycliste, ainsi que d’un trottoir de 2,00 à 2,50 m de large. Ce dernier est pavé et séparé de la voie cyclable par une pierre disposée en biais.


La Seenerstrasse est enjambée par un nouveau pont en béton armé de 23,50 m de long et 7,50 m de large. Conçu comme une structure à cadre, ce pont s’inspire visuellement du pont voisin des CFF.


L’eau de pluie s’infiltre en grande partie latéralement dans les bandes végétalisées adjacentes et l’ensemble du parcours est éclairé par des candélabres placés du côté nord. Des travaux de pose de conduites sont réalisés dans le cadre de ce projet.

title: DE01--ECO Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) Consolidated Effort - RFI (VA-27-00011677)
description: Request for Information Synopsis Enterprise Service Desk: Integrated Service Delivery Model with Independent Billing and Outcome Oversight 1.0 RFI Synopsis Narrative Background and Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Enterprise Command Operations (ECO) is issuing a Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research supporting a planned future acquisition strategy for Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) support and its associated Contact Center Infrastructure (CCI). VA currently operates ESD Tier 0/1 support and CCI as two separate prime contracts under a Multi-Vendor Service Provider (MVSP) model, where the CCI vendor produces independent Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance reporting and conducts formal quality assurance oversight of the Tier 1 vendor's performance. VA is exploring whether and how Tier 1 agent services and CCI platform management could be brought together under an integrated service delivery model, while determining what functions, if any, should remain organizationally independent from the delivery contractor to preserve objective performance, quality, and billing oversight. VA has not determined the appropriate scope or structure of any such independent function and is seeking industry input on whether independence is necessary, which functions require it, and the most effective means of providing it. The primary purpose of this RFI is to hear from industry on how an integrated delivery model would work in practice, i.e., how it would be structured, transitioned, and operated and to use that input, together with the Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimates requested below, to inform the resulting Performance Work Statement (PWS) and VA's decisions on scope, sequencing, and commercial structure. VA recognizes that consolidation may not be the right answer in every respect, and industry input that identifies where a combined model would be impractical, along with the reasoning behind that view, is just as valuable to VA as input on how to make consolidation work. This RFI is not a solicitation and does not commit VA to a particular acquisition approach. One specific issue on which VA would welcome industry input, particularly in the context of a combined model, is how outcomes should be classified if VA adopts outcome-based, automation-linked, or gainshare pricing. Under those pricing structures, the classification of individual contacts (e.g., AI-resolved vs. human-handled, genuinely deflected vs. merely relabeled, successfully automated vs. escalated) becomes the basis for what VA pays. If agent services and CCI are combined, VA wants to understand how a vendor would ensure that the entity performing the work and the entity classifying/reporting the outcome of that work don't create a structural incentive to classify ambiguous or borderline contacts in whichever direction favors billing. VA recognizes that transparent data feeds alone may not fully resolve this on their own, since the vendor typically controls the metadata structure, the correlation logic between systems, and the judgment calls in ambiguous cases. This lines up with feedback VA has already received from industry: multiple respondents to prior VA market research independently flagged the "AI-attempted-then-escalated" correlation and the "resolving tier" determination as fields that are self-reported, consequential to billing, and not easily produced by either vendor alone under the current structure. Given that feedback, VA wants industry's perspective on whether some form of independent validation of billing-relevant outcomes would be useful under a combined model, and if so, how narrowly or broadly it should be scoped. For example, whether it should focus solely on billing/outcome validation, or whether it makes more sense operationally to fold in general quality assurance scoring and day-to-day SLA compliance reporting as well. VA has not settled this question and is not assuming an independent function is necessary at all; VA's own data feeds, combined with automated QA tooling already in production, may prove sufficient on their own. This RFI invites industry input to help VA define the scope of the issue without presupposing a particular outcome. Strategic Direction VA's objective is not simply to combine two existing statements of work. It is to move the ESD operating model from a labor- and channel-centric structure to one organized around demand elimination, unified customer experience, and outcome-based accountability. Specifically, VA is seeking industry's perspective on an operating model that: Eliminates demand rather than optimizing contact handling. The strategic objective is not reducing cost per contact but reducing the volume of contacts that require human involvement in the first place, through AI-assisted self-service, proactive communication, automated fulfillment, and FboNotice-cause elimination. Presents a unified, channel-agnostic experience to the End User. The distinction between phone, chat, portal, and other channels should be invisible to the employee; the service environment, not the caller, determines whether AI, automation, knowledge, or a human agent is the appropriate resolution path. Treats AI and automation as the operating model, not an add-on. The relevant question is which categories of work should never require a human, and how the contractor is held contractually accountable for progressively moving categories of work off human agents. Realigns commercial incentives from resources consumed to outcomes achieved, while recognizing that outcome-based and gainshare pricing models raise the stakes on how outcomes are classified and who classifies them. Current Environment VA's current environment processes approximately 125,000 150,000 contacts per month across voice, chat, SMS, and self-service channels, supports roughly 600,000 End Users and 900 applications, and already has voice biometric verification, IVR-based automation (NICE Autopilot), and Medallia-based automated quality analytics in development or early production. VA's current CCI platform is NICE CXOne. VA is not presupposing that either of these existing tooling investments, the CCI platform or the automated QA platform, necessarily carries forward unchanged into a consolidated structure, and is asking industry to address both explicitly in the questions below. For purposes of responding to this RFI, the current functional baseline includes Tier 0/self-service and Tier 1 multi-channel end-user support, incident and service request intake, triage, resolution, and routing; knowledge management, process integration and new-service intake; workforce management, ACD/IVR and contact routing, contact recording and quality management, contact center platform administration; analytics and reporting; integration with VA's enterprise ITSM environment, customer experience capabilities, identity verification, existing voice AI/IVR automation and evolving enterprise self-service and AI capabilities; transition services; and continual service improvement. VA is interested in industry's perspective on evolving these capabilities toward an omnichannel service model and expanded AI-enabled automation. This description is intended to provide industry with sufficient context regarding the current functional baseline and potential scope under consideration. VA has not determined that all functions identified above will be included within a single future acquisition, nor has VA determined the final allocation of responsibilities among the delivery contractor, VA, other enterprise service providers, or any independent oversight function. Industry is specifically encouraged to identify functions that would benefit from common contractual accountability, as well as functions that should remain separate and the rationale for doing so. title: AFD - RFI - National Jewelry, Art, Antique, and Collectible (JAAC) Services
description: Background The U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) serves to protect, defend, and enforce the American justice system and is a key component within the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) Asset Forfeiture Program (AFP). Asset forfeiture plays a critical role in disrupting and dismantling illegal enterprises, depriving criminals of the proceeds of illegal activity, deterring crime, and restoring property to victims. As a component of the AFP, the USMS provides vital support to U.S. Attorney�s Offices and investigative agencies by assisting with pre-seizure planning and investigations. Additionally, the USMS serves as the primary custodial agency of the AFP. As part of its custodial responsibilities, the USMS inventories, manages, safeguards, and handles the disposition of seized and forfeited assets. Requirement and Request for Information The USMS has a specific requirement for the transport, intake, appraisal/authentication, storage, and disposal of seized and/or forfeited jewelry, art, antiques, and collectibles (JAAC) throughout the United States. The coverage area for these assets includes the 94 USMS Districts within the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. International services will likely be infrequent. The USMS is conducting market research through this Request for Information (RFI) for a potential solicitation in the coming months. RFI Submission Instructions If you are interested in this requirement, please provide a capability statement addressing your company�s ability to provide the needed services outlined within the enclosed draft JAAC Statement of Work. Please provide sufficient details regarding your company�s a) staff expertise, experience, and formal as well as other training; b) current in-house capability and capacity to perform the work; c) prior completed projects of similar nature; d) corporate experience and management capability; and e) examples of prior completed Government contracts, references, and other related information. In addition, all interested organizations should complete the JAAC RFI Questionnaire to provide additional details about your company and its capabilities. The Questionnaire can be found at the following link: https://usms.gov1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4U8liYnwfWxOqhw Further, complete the enclosed Pricing Schedule to provide your estimated prices/rates for the required services. When completing the pricing schedule, complete only the cells highlighted in yellow. Please do not submit a modified Pricing Schedule, only input estimated rates within the yellow cells. Note: The estimated rates provided will be for USMS market research only to obtain general knowledge of prices offered in the marketplace. Submission Deadline: All responses are due by 21 October 2026 by 10:00am EDT. Submit responses to ALL the following: Christopher Ottie (Contracting Officer) � Christopher.Ottie@usdoj.gov Millie Thomas (Contract Specialist) � Millie.Thomas@usdoj.gov AFP Procurement Team Inbox - AFP.Procurement@usdoj.gov Disclaimer This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this RFI is to identify sources, determine if interested organizations are capable of meeting the Government requirement, and to gather information regarding prices currently offered in the industry. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only.

Germany – Repair and maintenance services of security and defence materials – BG_1699_EU/26 - Werksinstandsetzung von Heizgerät des Systems SPz Marder
description: Der Auftrag umfasst die Werksinstandsetzung von Heizgerät des Systems SPz Marder. Die Bieter müssen im Rahmen der Angebotsabgabe berücksichtigen, dass die Angaben zu den jeweiligen Fachlosen lediglich aus den Vergangenheitswerten abgeleitete Schätzbedarfe sind sowie einen gegebenenfalls auftretenden Mehrbedarf (Sicherheitszuschlag) enthalten. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet nach 4 Jahren. Wenn der bestehende Vertrag zwischen der HIL GmbH und der Bundeswehr, egal aus welchem Rechtsgrund endet, kann die Rahmenvereinbarung durch ein Sonderkündigungsrecht beendet werden.

title: Netherlands – Endangered species protection services – Natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) en een gebiedsdekkend (Pré) Soortenmanagementplan (SMP)
description: Gemeente Beekdaelen beoogt met deze aanbestedingsprocedure een gebiedsdekkend soortenmanagementplan (SMP), een pré-SMP en de uitvoering van natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) te verwerven, inclusief begeleiding van de bijbehorende aanvragen omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag. Gemeente Beekdaelen beoogt met deze aanbestedingsprocedure een gebiedsdekkend soortenmanagementplan (SMP), een pré-SMP en de uitvoering van natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) te verwerven, inclusief begeleiding van de bijbehorende aanvragen omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag. De opdracht bestaat uit één overeenkomst voor de ontwikkeling van drie onderdelen. 1. Het uitvoeren van de opdracht Natuurvriendelijk isoleren voor gemeente Beekdaelen; 2. Het ontwikkelen van een Pré-Soortenmangementplan, inclusief het verzorgen en begeleiden van de bijbehorende aanvraagprocedure voor een (tijdelijke) omgevingsvergunning voor een flora- en faunactiviteit bij het bevoegd gezag en ondersteuning bij eventuele bezwaar- en beroepsprocedures voor Gemeente Beekdaelen; 3. Het ontwikkelen van een gebiedsdekkend SMP, inclusief het verzorgen en begeleiden van de bijbehorende aanvraagprocedure voor een gebiedsgerichte omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna-activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag en ondersteuning bij eventuele bezwaar- en beroepsprocedures voor de gemeente Beekdaelen. Beekdaelen telt ongeveer 35.903 inwoners met ongeveer 16.915 woningen. Hiervan zijn 72,8% koopwoningen. Gemeente Beekdaelen heeft een totale oppervlakte van 7.840 hectare en de gemiddelde dichtheid van de adressen is 508 adressen per km2. Het onderzoek richt zich op het bebouwde gebied. Dit bedraagt ongeveer 12.6 km². Het onderzoeksgebied dient als basis voor de prijsvorming. Het definitieve onderzoeksgebied zal in samenspraak met de Provincie Limburg moeten worden vastgesteld gedurende de eerste fase van de opdracht. Gemeente Beekdaelen wenst binnen drie jaar na opdrachtverstrekking het NVI te hebben voltooid en te beschikken over een goed werkend SMP, inclusief een gebiedsgerichte omgevingsvergunning.

title: FCI Elkton - Upgrade Fire Pump
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Elkton, anticipates the issuance of a solicitation for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project titled Upgrade Fire Pump for FCI Elkton located 8730 Scroggs Road, Lisbon, OH 44432. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation prepared in accordance with the format in subpart FAR Revision Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes as the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation is issued (see attached). You are required to provide all pages of the written attached solicitation with your complete quotation. Solicitation Number: 15BBNF26Q21600002 and is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) A statement that the solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-1, Effective Date March 13, 2026. This is a 100 percent small business set-aside. You must be registered in www.sam.gov as a small business for the applicable NAICS code. (see FAR Provision 52.219-1 in the Representations and Certifications section of your sam.gov registration). The Period of Performance for this project will be 181 Calendar Days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed. The provision at 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition and a statement regarding any addenda to the provision. All quotes will be evaluated based on price, technical capability, and past performance. Clause at 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition. SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, tools, and incidentals necessary to remove the existing diesel fire pump controller and associated components and furnish and install a new UL?listed diesel fire pump controller in a NEMA 4/4X enclosure. Work includes demolition of obsolete battery racks, conduit, and wiring; installation of new underground conduit and communication lines; reconnection of engine control circuits, sensors, and dual?battery systems; and integration with the facility�s Siemens DDC and Desigo CC automation platforms. All work must be performed in compliance with NFPA 20, applicable Federal, State, and local codes, and Bureau of Prisons technical requirements. Commissioning will include hydrostatic testing, flow/no?flow testing, controller functional checks, and alarm/signal verification. See the attached Statement of Work and Drawings for complete technical specifications. The estimated magnitude of the project is between $250,000 and $500,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 238210 (Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors) with a corresponding small business size standard of $19.0 million average annual receipts for the firms preceding three fiscal years. The solicitation will only be distributed soley through the Contract Opportunity website at https://www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions for documents. The "Sensitive/Secure Package Upload" option will be selected for this procurement. All secure/locked documents upload, to include the solicitation will require an active SAM vendor registration to obtain access. In addition, only those vendors who have been issued a valid Marketing Pamer Identification Number (MPIN) from www.sam.gov will be granted access. If your firm does not have the NAICS code listed in www.sam.gov required for this solicitation, an email may be forwarded to your firm requesting an explanation as to why your firm should be granted access. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendment will also be distributed soley through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. IMPORTANT: Any contractor interested in doing business with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered in https://www.sam.gov. In order to qualify for award, your business size metrics information entered in your SAM registration will be reviewed by the Government to confirm your size business size meets the small business size standard requirement. All quoters are urged to double check their SAM registration and update as necessary, including the size metrics information. SITE VISIT: An organized site visit has been scheduled for Wednesday, October 7, at 9:00 am EDT with Mr. George Holisky, at FCI Elkton, 8730 Scroggs Road, Lisbon, OH 44432. Please see the attached Instructions to Offerors for requirements and further information. SUBMISSION OF QUOTES: All quotes will be submitted electronically via email to lbonner@bop.gov no later than October 21, 2026 at 11:00 am EDT.

title: Upper Wicomico River Dredging Project, Wicomico County, MD
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Baltimore District will be completing maintenance dredging in the upper half of the Wicomico River, Wicomico County, MD. Material will be placed at an existing upland placement site near the river named Sharps Point located in Salisbury, MD. The Magnitude of Construction is $4,000,000.00 to $8,000,000.00. The construction duration will be approximately 120 calendar days from Notice to Proceed.The scope includes using a hydraulic dredge and pipeline in the upper portion of the Wicomico River to remove material to its authorized depth of 14 feet. Approximately 250,000 cubic yards of material consisting of silts, sand, clays, mixed shell, gravel and other materials will be dredged and placed at the Sharps Point site. Minor construction of two weir boxes will also occur at the placement site prior to dredging operations.
